text: Compliance asks a direct question: show us every system storing customer Social Security Numbers, and prove each one is classified and controlled. This is the test everything since Lesson 8 has been building toward.
Our classification export answers it in one query: one column, in veridian-sql-prod, correctly labeled and correctly access-controlled. It looks complete.

The auditor doesn't accept that. Is this list based on what Purview scanned, or on every table that actually exists? That question sends us straight to Oracle's own schema catalog, independent of Purview.

There it is: CUSTOMERS_RAW.SSN, a real column Purview has never seen, because Lesson 8 only registered the reporting view sitting on top of it. The view was built honestly. It just hid a table underneath.
One system has unprotected customer SSNs we didn't know about. Next: register it, lock it down, and fix the process gap that let it go unnoticed.
